covers.quote: You must make sure content is clear

rules.quote: Make sure content uses plain language.
rules.specification: The page supplies no reading-level threshold or operational definition of plain language. Treat the general clarity statement as supporting this requirement, not as a second finding for the same language problem. Use the more specific unusual-expression and acronym rules for those defects.
rules.violation_condition: The language is unnecessarily difficult for the intended audience to understand.
when: Clarity is expressly mandatory for content subject to the Digital Service Standard.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the overlapping clarity wording; the more specific vocabulary and acronym checks remain separate.

covers.quote: You must make sure content is clear, accurate and consistent to meet the Digital Service Standard:

rules.quote: You must make sure content is consistent
rules.specification: The page requires consistency but does not specify which dimensions must be checked or how intentional variations should be distinguished from errors.
rules.violation_condition: Comparable parts of the content use inconsistent language or style without a contextual reason for the variation.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the repeated consistency requirement; consistency is distinct from clarity, structure and correctness.

rules.quote: You must make sure content is consistent, has a clear structure and is error free to make it accessible for all users.
rules.specification: This item captures only the clear-structure requirement in the quoted sentence. The page does not define a test for structural clarity or prescribe a particular heading hierarchy.
rules.violation_condition: The content lacks a clear organisation or hierarchy through which users can follow its information.
rules.why: The grain test separates structural clarity from the sentence's independently checkable consistency and correctness requirements.

covers.quote: You must make sure content is clear, accurate and consistent to meet the Digital Service Standard:
The master copy should be error-free so the proofreader can check for any introduced errors.

rules.quote: You must make sure content is consistent, has a clear structure and is error free to make it accessible for all users.
rules.specification: This item captures the general accuracy and error-free requirement, not the separate consistency or structure requirements. The page does not define an error taxonomy or a factual-verification method, so it does not by itself specify an implementable correctness check.
rules.violation_condition: The content contains an error or inaccurate information.
when: The approved master copy used for proofreading is also expressly expected to be error-free.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates accuracy and error-free wording; G-2 retains the master-copy application without creating a second correctness finding.

rules.quote: Avoid (or explain) unusual words, phrases and idioms.
rules.specification: Assess whether an expression is unusual for the intended audience rather than against a universal prohibited-word list. The page does not prescribe where its explanation must appear.
rules.violation_condition: An unusual word, phrase or idiom appears without an explanation that makes it understandable to the intended audience.
when: An unusual word, phrase or idiom may be used if it is explained.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3 keep avoidance and the explanation exception together as one check.

rules.quote: Expand all acronyms on their first use.
rules.violation_condition: An acronym's first occurrence in the content has no expansion.
when: Check the first use of each acronym in the content.
rules.why: The grain test keeps the concrete first-use expansion check separate from general plain-language advice.

rules.quote: Make sure other content elements, including captions, transcripts, alt text, link text, headings and instructions are accessible to all users.
rules.specification: This is a high-level requirement about the accessibility of supporting text. The sentence does not define an operational accessibility test; the WCAG titles elsewhere on the page should not be expanded into unstated rules.
rules.violation_condition: A supporting textual element is inaccessible to users.
when: Applies to captions, transcripts, alt text, link text, headings, instructions and comparable supporting textual elements.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the listed element types as cases of one accessibility requirement; this concerns text rather than the editing workflow.
